lead: The oldest, most bohemian and most vibrant district in Valencia. A unique cocktail of medieval walls, street art, avant-garde museums and squares full of Mediterranean life.

El Carmen, at the north-western end of Ciutat Vella, is the best-known and most visited district in Valencia. It takes its name from the church and convent of the Carmen Calzado and has more than a thousand years of history: it was an Arab suburb outside the walls in the 11th century, it came inside the city with the Christian extension of the wall in the 14th century and has since been a refuge for the most varied medieval guilds.

Today El Carmen is a perfect combination of medieval architecture, Arab walls built into houses, modern and contemporary art museums, one of the largest street art galleries in Spain and the epicentre of Valencian nightlife. All in a compact area that can be covered entirely on foot.

items.title: Serranos Towers
items.subtitle: The north gate of the walled city · 14th century
items.body: The Serranos Towers are the most imposing gate remaining from Valencia’s old medieval wall. Built between 1392 and 1398 by master builder Pere Balaguer, these 33-metre-high polygonal towers were for centuries the main entrance to the city from the north, the road towards the mountains. Inside, several vaulted rooms are preserved, and from the battlements you get some of the best panoramic views of the Turia Garden and the old town.
facts: 33 metres · Panoramic views from the battlements
It served as a prison for nobles between the 16th and 19th centuries

items.title: Quart Towers
items.subtitle: The western gate · Napoleonic scars on the façade
items.body: The Quart Towers close off El Carmen to the west. Built between 1441 and 1468, they are the best-preserved Gothic defensive towers in Europe. Their most singular feature is their outer façade, which still bears the marks of the cannon fire of the Napoleonic siege of 1808: 132 cannonball impacts and more than 1,000 perforations from rifle projectiles, scars of Valencian resistance that it was decided to preserve during the restoration.
facts: 34 metres · One metre taller than the Serranos Towers
The marks of the 1808 Napoleonic cannon fire are preserved on the façade

items.title: Portal de la Valldigna
items.subtitle: Former access to the morería · Arab 11th century · Christian 15th
items.body: The Portal de la Valldigna is one of the most photogenic corners of El Carmen, and one of the richest in history. This semicircular arch, built on the 11th-century Islamic wall, separated Christian Valencia from the morería in the Middle Ages, the district where Muslims were concentrated after James I’s Reconquista. The portal takes its name from the Cistercian Monastery of Santa María de Valldigna, whose procurator’s house stood opposite it.
facts: It separated the Christian city from the medieval morería
A few metres away, Lamberto Palmart set up the first printing press in Spain (1474)
Free · C/ de la Valldigna · Centre of the district

items.kicker: Cultural centre · Free access to exhibitions
items.title: Centre del Carme Cultura Contemporània
items.subtitle: Former Carmen Convent · Gothic and Renaissance cloisters
items.body: The Centre del Carme Cultura Contemporània occupies the former Convent of Our Lady of Carmen, which gives the district its name. The building, which was also home to the School of Fine Arts and Crafts, preserves two spectacular cloisters: a Gothic one from the 14th century and a Renaissance one from the 16th. Today it is a cultural reference point in Valencia, with exhibitions of visual arts, performing arts, performance, music and one of the city’s most dynamic contemporary art programmes.
facts: Former Carmen Convent · Gothic (14th c.) and Renaissance (16th c.) cloister
Visual arts, performance, music and performing arts
Many exhibitions with free access · Check the programme
Plaza del Carmen · Heart of the district

items.title: IVAM · Institut Valencià d’Art Modern
items.subtitle: The most important modern art museum in the Comunitat
items.body: The Institut Valencià d’Art Modern is the great avant-garde museum of El Carmen and one of the most prestigious in Spain. Its permanent collection exceeds 12,000 works by Spanish and international artists: painting, sculpture, drawing, photography, video and installation. Artists represented include Julio González, Antoni Tàpies, Yves Klein, Tony Cragg, Carmen Calvo, Manolo Valdés and Fernando Arroyo. On Friday afternoons admission is free.
facts: C/ de la Beneficencia, 2 · Next to El Carmen district

items.title: Arab Wall and Civil War Shelters
items.subtitle: 11th-century Islamic · Shelters of the capital of the Republic
items.body: El Carmen is the place where the remains of the 11th-century Arab wall are most visible, because the district grew up behind it, preserving and integrating its sections and towers into the buildings. Remains can be seen in the Plaza del Ángel and Plaza de los Navarros, in Calle de la Cruz, in Plaza del Tossal and inside the historic Horno Montaner. In addition, Valencia was the capital of the Second Republic during part of the Civil War, and at number 25 Calle Serrans and number 37 Calle Alta are the city’s air-raid shelters.
facts: 11th century · Remains in Plaza del Tossal, Plaza del Ángel and Calle de la Cruz
Arab tower built into the building · Declared a National Monument (1963)
C/ Serrans, 25 and C/ Alta, 37 · Valencia, capital of the Republic
Wall remains are visible on the street · Shelters with guided visit

items.title: Street Art · The Street of Colours
items.subtitle: Murals, graffiti and street art · Calle Moret and surroundings
items.body: El Carmen is one of the largest open-air street-art galleries in Spain. Calle Moret, known as the Street of Colours, is its main axis: large-format murals, graffiti with social content and works by local artists such as Escif or Vinilo turn every façade into a canvas. Street art is also concentrated on Calle Baja, Calle Alta and around Plaza del Tossal. The offering changes with the seasons: every walk is different from the last.
facts: Calle Moret · The main axis of El Carmen street art
Escif, Vinilo and dozens of local and international artists
C/ Baja, C/ Alta, Plaza del Tossal and around the IVAM
Completely free · The display changes each season

items.title: Squares and Food in El Carmen
items.subtitle: Plaza del Negrito · Plaza del Árbol · Plaza del Carmen · Calle Caballeros
items.body: The squares of El Carmen are the social heart of the district and of Valencian nightlife. Plaza del Negrito concentrates bars and local rhythm until the small hours. Plaza del Árbol is a quieter corner with charm. Plaza del Carmen, opposite the former convent, has terraces perfect for a coffee. Calle Caballeros is the main food artery. The “Agua de Valencia” — orange juice, cava and vodka — was invented here, at the Café de las Horas (Conde de Almodóvar, 1).
facts: Epicentre of nightlife · Bars and terraces until the small hours
Orange juice + cava + vodka · Invented at the Café de las Horas
Look for the hidden Arab dead-end alleys in the district

blocks.title: Tips for visiting El Carmen district
items: The Serranos and Quart Towers have free admission all year round: ideal for starting your visit
The IVAM is free on Friday afternoons: the best time to visit without queues
The Centre del Carme has many exhibitions with free access: check the programme before you go
The district is entirely pedestrian and flat: perfect for exploring by bike with Valenbisi
For street art, start at Calle Moret (the Street of Colours) and continue towards Plaza del Tossal
The original Agua de Valencia is drunk at the Café de las Horas (Conde de Almodóvar, 1) · Open from midday
